messages.message: ### Step 2: Morphosyntactic Requirement Definition Goal: For Telugu, specify per-token morphosyntax needed to realize the Step 1 Interpretation Lock. Requirements (ONE Markdown table): - Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Requirement] - In [Target Requirement], make comparative direction unambiguous and add a 1-line literal back-translation check. Output: ONLY the table; no extra prose.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition | Target Requirement (Telugu) | |-------------|----------------------|------------------------------| | Nel | “in the middle of” (locative phrase) | Use locative case – **మధ్యలో** (mid‑in). **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “midway”. | | mezzo | “middle” (noun) | Noun **మధ్య** in locative when combined with “Nel”. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “middle”. | | del | genitive “of the” linking road to life | Genitive marker **‑కు** on “road” → **పథానికి**. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “of the”. | | cammin | “road, path” (metaphor for life’s course) | Noun **పథం** in genitive case (**పథానికి**). **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “road”. | | di | “of” (genitive preposition) | Expressed by the same genitive case **‑కు** on the head noun. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “of”. | | nostra | “our” (possessive adjective) | Possessive pronoun **మా** agreeing with feminine singular **జీవితం**. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “our”. | | vita | “life” (noun) | Noun **జీవితం** in genitive (**జీవితానికి**) to show possession. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “life”. | | mi | Reflexive pronoun “myself” (object) | Accusative pronoun **నన్ను** attached to verb. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “myself”. | | ritrovai | “found” (1st‑person singular perfect) | Verb **కనుగొన్నాను** – past tense, first person, perfective aspect. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “found”. | | per | Preposition “within/through” | Post‑position **లో** attached to following noun (locative). **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “within”. | | una | Indefinite article “a” (non‑specific) | No article in Telugu; noun remains singular. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “a”. | | selva | “forest, wood” (noun) | Noun **అడవి** in locative case (**అడవిలో**) due to “per”. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “forest”. | | oscura | “dark” (adjective) | Adjective **చీకటి** agreeing with feminine singular noun, placed before noun (**చీకటి అడవి**). **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “dark”. | | ché | Conjunction “for/because” | Causal conjunction **ఎందుకంటే**. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “for”. | | la | Definite article “the” (not lexical in Telugu) | Omitted; noun carries case marker. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “the”. | | diritta | “right, correct” (adjective) | Adjective **సరైన** agreeing with feminine singular noun **వైపు**. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “right”. | | via | “way, path” (noun, subject of clause) | Noun **వైపు** in nominative (subject). **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “way”. | | era | “was” (3rd‑person singular imperfect) | Auxiliary verb **ఉంది** in past imperfect (**ఉన్నది**). **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “was”. | | smarrita | “missed, lost” (past participle) | Past participle **కోల్పోయింది** agreeing with feminine singular **వైపు**; used with auxiliary **ఉంది**. **Comparative direction:** N/A. **Back‑translation check:** “missed”. |

### Step 3: Pre-assembled Lexical Inventory Create placeable Telugu components for Step 4. Output ONLY bullet list; ONE LINE per bullet. - Line <ID>: <Phrase 1> / <Phrase 2> / <Phrase 3> Where <ID> is the leading integer at the start of the source line. Hook: each phrase must satisfy the Step 2 Requirements table for that line (including the literal back-translation checks). Rules: Each phrase is directly placeable in the final line (no glue-only fragments). Must keep the line’s main predicate + any required linkage (result/purpose/relative); do not output only a subordinate fragment. Avoid embedding clause-linking connectors inside a phrase; keep phrases as clean, placeable propositions and let Step 4 add any necessary linking function-words/morphology. For comparatives, preserve direction and include comparator/degree in the phrase. No punctuation characters inside phrases; keep phrases short; no newlines.

- Line 1: మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో / మన జీవితం మార్గం మధ్యలో / మన జీవితం పథం మధ్యలో - Line 2: నేను చీకటి అడవిలో కనుగొన్నాను / నేను చీకటి అడవిలో తాను కనుగొన్నాను / నేను చీకటి అడవిలో తాను కనిపించాను - Line 3: సరైన మార్గం కోల్పోయింది / సరైన పథం కోల్పోయింది / సరైన దారి కోల్పోయింది

### Step 4: Slot-Based Syntactic Assembly Assemble Step3 components into Telugu lines; keep the same number of lines. Use Step3 Final Form as contiguous substrings; reorder within-line as needed. If simple concatenation is ungrammatical or produces a predicate-clash, you MAY insert only function-words and/or inflectional morphology needed for grammatical joining; do NOT add new content words. When adding linking function-words/morphology, match the relation implied by the source line (result/purpose/relative) and do NOT turn it into a contrast relation unless the source explicitly contrasts. Semantic completeness: each Target Text MUST express the full Locked Meaning for that Source Line; do NOT drop the main predicate when the line contains a main predicate + linked clause. Punctuation: copy ONLY end punctuation from the source line to the END of Target Text; add NO internal punctuation. For each source line output ONLY this block (labels verbatim): Source Line: <copy exact source line> Line Inventory: - <copy the phrases you chose from Step 3 for this line> Assembly Notes: - If you inserted any function-words/morphology for joining, list them briefly. Target Text: <assembled target line> If you forgot a necessary phrase from Step 3: re-insert it (no new content words).

Source Line: 1 Nel mezzo del cammin di nostra vita Line Inventory: - మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో Assembly Notes: - none Target Text: మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో
Source Line: 2 mi ritrovai per una selva oscura, Line Inventory: - నేను చీకటి అడవిలో తాను కనుగొన్నాను Assembly Notes: - none Target Text: నేను చీకటి అడవిలో తాను కనుగొన్నాను,
Source Line: 3 ché la diritta via era smarrita. Line Inventory: - సరైన మార్గం కోల్పోయింది Assembly Notes: - none Target Text: సరైన మార్గం కోల్పోయింది.

### Step 5: Self-Correction via Back-Translation & Grammatical Check Verify each Step4 line vs Reference Translation + Locked Meaning; correct within-line only. Allowed: reorder within the line; re-insert only Step4 Missing; fix function-word/morphology anywhere; never add new content words; never move across lines. Punctuation rule: do NOT introduce new internal punctuation; only keep the end punctuation transferred from the source line. Per line output bullets with EXACT fields: - Line #: <ID> - Target Text (from Step 4): <...> - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): <...> - Reference Translation (line-aligned): <...> - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct <OK|FAIL>, Coverage <OK|FAIL>, Meaning Drift <OK|FAIL>, Comparative Orientation <OK|FAIL|N/A>, Hallucination <OK|FAIL> - If any FAIL: Corrected Target Text: <...> End Punct: compare last non-whitespace char of Target Text vs Source Line. Line # rule: <ID> is the leading integer at the start of that Source Line. After all lines: if any FAIL, label final as UNVERIFIED and list failing Line # values. Output final Telugu text in ONE code block, line by line.

- Line #: 1 - Target Text (from Step 4): మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): midway the road of our life - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): Midway upon the road of our life - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 2 - Target Text (from Step 4): నేను చీకటి అడవిలో తాను కనుగొన్నాను, - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): I within dark forest myself found , - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): I found myself within a dark wood, - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **OK**, Meaning Drift **OK**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK**
- Line #: 3 - Target Text (from Step 4): సరైన మార్గం కోల్పోయింది. - Back-Translation (literal into the reference translation's language): the right way lost . - Reference Translation (line‑aligned): for the right way had been missed. - Checks (OK/FAIL): End Punct **OK**, Coverage **FAIL**, Meaning Drift **FAIL**, Comparative Orientation **N/A**, Hallucination **OK** - Corrected Target Text: ఎందుకంటే సరైన మార్గం కోల్పోయింది.
**FINAL STATUS:** UNVERIFIED (Failing Line #: 3)
```telugu మన జీవితం యొక్క మార్గం మధ్యలో నేను చీకటి అడవిలో తాను కనుగొన్నాను, ఎందుకంటే సరైన మార్గం కోల్పోయింది. ```
